lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is Tuesday's BOCC meeting, where San Miguel County takes up two Land Use Code amendments — one on natural medicine businesses and one on nonconforming lots, the kind of quiet code language that determines what gets built and where for years to come. Wednesday brings the county's sixth housing code working session, drilling into zoning, density, and incentives as staff moves toward final redline recommendations. Meanwhile, HARC sits down Tuesday with the multi-building Carhenge redevelopment at 700 W Pacific — preliminary large-scale public hearings on a project that would reshape a significant chunk of Backman Village.
